title: Promising Results - Update #1
author: Weak_Wallaby734
selftext:
Figured I’d post an update since a few people were interested in how things were progressing.

For those who didn’t see my original post, I built an automated trading bot for Kalshi’s 15-minute crypto markets using Claude. Started with $50 and have been continuously refining and scaling the system.

Well, we’re now sitting at **over $3,000**.  
I’ll attach some updated screenshots so you guys can see the results yourselves.

A few things have changed since my original post.  
I’ve continued refining the execution, risk management, and overall efficiency of the bot. It’s running completely autonomously, 24/7, and I’ve been gradually scaling as the account grows.  
I’ve also experienced some losses along the way. I’m not going to pretend the system is perfect or unbeatable. 

One thing I’ve learned is that a high win rate doesn’t necessarily mean low risk, especially when a single loss can erase numerous winning trades.

That being said, I’m pretty happy with how it’s performing.  
One interesting aspect is that the strategy uses maker orders, allowing me to trade without execution fees under the current fee structure. That’s been an important part of the system’s performance.

My next goal is to build a larger account cushion before shifting my focus toward periodically withdrawing profits rather than continuously compounding.

I’m still actively monitoring performance, execution quality, and how the strategy behaves under different market conditions.  
And just to clarify, I’m not selling anything, offering subscriptions, or sharing the underlying strategy. This is simply a personal project I’ve been developing with AI assistance.

Still a long way to go before I’d consider anything definitively proven, but it’s been an interesting experiment so far.  
I’ll continue posting updates as things progress, whether good or bad.

Cheers.

comments.author: Zain_One
comments.body:
This is actually interesting, especially the point you made about one loss potentially wiping out a lot of winning trades. I think that’s probably more important than the headline win rate.

Going from $50 to $3k is obviously a strong run, but I’d be curious about the risk side now that you have a decent sample and things like max drawdown, your worst individual loss, and how the P&L looks if you remove the few best days/trades. Also curious about the maker-order side. Are you seeing any meaningful adverse selection there? As in, getting filled more often when the market is about to move against you, while missing some of the better moves because your limit never gets hit?

No need to share the actual strategy obviously. Would just be interesting to know what you’re seeing from the execution/risk data as you scale it. 

Nice project either way, and respect for posting the losses as well as the wins. 👍

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body: My fill rate is about 90%+ and market going against me doesn’t necessarily mean I’ll get force filled. It could trigger my other features, that pull the order. And it’ll sit on a partial fill which losses overall for almost 3 full weeks of 24/7 days on V2 I’m extremely happy. I’m roughly 2 months total of data logged and a lot of tweaks.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Good that you're open about the tail risk. A high win rate can hide a big loss. Since the edge comes from maker orders, I'd watch adverse selection: the orders that fill are often the ones the price then moves against, while the ones that don't fill are the winners. It's worth comparing results on filled versus unfilled orders, and checking how the account would look if the fee rules changed. If you want to test bot changes without risking money, Cymetica lets you run AI agents in paper mode on a practice balance.

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body: If fee rules change my method is not worth doing. I’ve found that using real money real account gives me best results. Currently just under 10k logged trades saved to my external ssd. I have them organized by day, week, month. What news was active. I also run the data through Claude again and see if I should make more changes

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Nearly 10k logged trades is a strong base, and most people never get close to that. One thing to watch when you run the data back through Claude is that it can always find a pattern that fits the past. I'd change one thing at a time and judge it only on the trades made after the change, not on the old ones. That way you can tell a real improvement from a fit to old data.

replies.author: Weak_Wallaby734
replies.body: It’s exactly how I’m doing it.
